The first OPF you can install: one installer puts in the slicer and the farm, and OPF is OPF everywhere, from the program's name to the icon on the taskbar.

**Download:** `OPF_Setup_0.2.0_x64.exe` below, for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). Windows may say it protected your PC, because OPF is not code-signed yet: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*. The portable zip runs without installing.

## What is in 0.2.0

- **One installer for everything.** OPF Slicer (OrcaSlicer with the farm built in) and the farm program come together. Open **OPF** from the Start menu; the farm starts with it and stays by the clock.
- **Before each print.** Every printer has boxes for bed levelling, flow calibration, resonance compensation and timelapse, used by every plate it starts.
- **Plates named after their parts.** A plate nobody named goes into the queue under its part's name, not as Untitled.
- **One window.** *Open OPF* in the tray brings the open slicer forward instead of starting another.
- **OPF everywhere.** The program is `OPF.exe`, the icon is the shelf on a white tile so it shows on a dark taskbar, and the slicer says OPF where it said OrcaSlicer (its credits stay, as the licence asks).
- **Its own settings.** OPF keeps its settings in `%APPDATA%\OPF Slicer`, started from a copy of OrcaSlicer's the first time, so an installed OrcaSlicer is left as it is.
- **Updates.** An installed OPF checks for a new release every few hours and offers the download page.

## Good to know

- Bambu Lab printers need LAN mode, and Developer Mode for OPF to start prints. A1 and A1 mini are in daily use; P1 and X1 use the same protocol but have been tested less.
- Anycubic Kobra 3, 3 Max and S1 support is new: watch the first print.
- Some of OrcaSlicer's rarely used dialogs may still use its name.

Source: [the farm](https://github.com/Artis-98/opf/tree/v0.2.0) and [OPF Slicer](https://github.com/Artis-98/opf-slicer/tree/v0.2.0), both under the GNU AGPL 3.0. Built by GitHub Actions from that source.
